name: MarkLab capability map
scope: Implemented public workflows, method families, data contracts and command routes in this checkout. Methods are grouped rather than enumerating every Rust type or option. Uses are representative combinations, not an exhaustive list of possible scientific questions.

reading_guide.capabilities: What each family does, consumes, produces and currently connects to.
reading_guide.interactions: Implemented end-to-end flows versus combinations requiring explicit user orchestration.
reading_guide.applications: Possible questions and the capabilities to combine; not validated biological or clinical claims.
reading_guide.command_index: Complete source-declared leaf command names by prefix; use marklab <prefix> <command> --help for arguments. Root commands omit the prefix. Built-in help and private worker entrypoints are excluded.
reading_guide.sources: Repository-relative paths; evidence statements summarize existing documentation, not scientific checks rerun for this inventory.

interfaces.rust: marklab root exports plus spatial, structure, marks, autocorrelation, compartments, embeddings, workflow, pathology and backend modules; companion crates expose additional scientific APIs.
interfaces.cli: marklab with the cli Cargo feature; defaults also enable parallel, csv and parquet.
interfaces.python_client: Thin subprocess client for multiplex studies and pathology architecture; explicit cell-table, AnnData and selected upstream adapters. Not a Python binding for every Rust API.
interfaces.python_workers: Selected model, registration, topology and prediction commands use the repository's locked Python 3.12 runtime.

optional_features.wsi: Slide metadata and bounded RGBA region reading via wsi-rs.
optional_features.parquet: Cell-table Parquet and strict embedding Arrow IPC/Parquet profiles.
optional_features.csv: Cell tables and normalized CSV adapters.

shared_contracts.identity: Explicit patient/site/specimen/block/core/slide/section/region/cell/patch/timepoint IDs, hierarchy and replication roles; coordinates and measurements stay bound to their objects.
shared_contracts.coordinates: Declared physical units, coordinate frames, axis/image conventions and transforms; no implicit pixel-to-micrometre conversion or registration.
shared_contracts.observations: Binary, probability, categorical, ordinal, continuous, assay and vector marks; missingness and measured/imported-prediction/morphology-prediction/derived-summary status remain explicit.
shared_contracts.geometry: Observation-window polygons/multipolygons can preserve holes and disconnected pieces; each method has its own geometry and edge-correction restrictions.
shared_contracts.inference: Null model, exchangeability unit, strata, support, seed and multiplicity family are part of the scientific design. Random labeling, fixed-count spatial simulations and model-based posterior prediction answer different questions.
shared_contracts.availability: Unavailable/disabled/failed/nonconverged values have explicit status or errors; missing results are not scientific zeros.
shared_contracts.reproducibility: Fixed inputs, settings, seed, implementation and numerical environment support replay; universal cross-platform bitwise identity is not claimed.
shared_contracts.resources: Method-specific input, memory, work, graph, geometry, simulation and worker-time budgets; admission estimates are not measured performance guarantees.
shared_contracts.publication: Analysis/study directories publish transactionally. Utilities have their own file contracts. Durable projects reuse compatible completed results and invalidate dependent work when inputs change.
shared_contracts.results: The current root result.json contract is 0.5; its reader accepts the current version. Specialized methods have separate versioned documents. This inventory changes no result format.

does: Bounded materialized AnnData/H5AD including sparse round trips
Optional normalized CellViT CSV/NPY and bundle profiles
input_adapters.input: Upstream cells, annotations or vectors plus IDs, calibration, window, patient grouping and producer declarations.
input_adapters.output: Validated patterns, study slides, architecture recipes or embedding artifacts.
input_adapters.used_by: analyze/classical/batch, multimodal, study, pathology architecture and embedding workflows; adapters are specific contracts, not universal native-format readers.
uses: Analyze outputs from a chosen segmentation/embedding model
Normalize multiplex platforms into a common patient-level study
input_adapters.limits: AnnData backed/lazy arrays are unsupported. QuPath nucleus and architecture profiles differ. Generic embeddings do not require CellViT's dimension/calibration. Explicit mapping is required for unsupported native exports.

whole_slide_access.input: Supported WSI file and explicit scene/level/plane/region.
whole_slide_access.output: Metadata JSON or decoded region pixels/image.
uses: Extract regions for external image processing or visual review
whole_slide_access.limits: No WSI writer, cell segmentation, viewer-state import or general OME-XML semantic/calibration adapter. Public pixel agreement is scoped to the tested Aperio region.

does: Permutation-whitened mark spectrum and low-frequency excess
Tapered FFT periodogram and scale-energy curves
Multiscale residual maps and connected territories
marked_section.input: Cell coordinates, binary/probabilistic marks, tissue mask and TOML configuration; declared scalar API additionally binds identity/status/provenance.
marked_section.output: Marked-pattern JSON with primary endpoint, curves/envelopes, territories, QC and availability; configurable Parquet curves, GeoJSON territories, figures and run manifest.
marked_section.used_by: AnalysisEngine -> analyze/batch -> OutputWriter; marked workflow nodes and pre/post DAG reuse the same engine. Internal spectral helpers are not separate supported public modules.
uses: Detect clustered, dispersed or directional labeling
Check whether spatial strata explain a label pattern
marked_section.limits: Conditions on observed cell geometry and declared exchangeability; a significant label pattern does not establish clonality or cause. Each curve envelope covers its own eligible scale family, not every marker/run.

does: Marked pre/post endpoint and curve comparisons
prepost_and_batch.input: Manifest rows or compatible completed pre/post analyses, with matching scientific identities and settings.
prepost_and_batch.output: Per-analysis outputs or change/comparison summaries with availability and margin assessments.
prepost_and_batch.used_by: batch, prepost, multimodal batch/prepost; Rust comparison functions; project marked-prepost and marked pre/post DAG.
prepost_and_batch.limits: Sections contain different cells; this is not cell tracking or evidence of a treatment effect. Population inference requires a patient-level design.

does: Homogeneous K/L with border, translation or isotropic correction
Homogeneous g with standard, translation or isotropic correction
Nearest-neighbor G, empty-space F and J
point_patterns_2d.input: 2-D points, exact observed window, radii/bins, edge policy and optional types/intensities/compartments; declared simulation or labeling null.
point_patterns_2d.output: Radius-indexed curves, pair/support counts, intensity diagnostics and optional envelopes/p-values.
point_patterns_2d.used_by: marklab::spatial; classical/nearest-space; project spatial routes; pathology spatial-study. Global envelopes use marklab-numerics.
point_patterns_2d.limits: CSR relocates cells; random labeling fixes them. Inhomogeneous cross-K is not implemented. Edge/normalization conventions matter; single-type inhomogeneous g lacks independent reference agreement. Public agreement applies to documented observed estimators, not every inferential configuration.

does: Categorical enrichment with exact fixed-count null moments and Monte Carlo inference
Soft neighborhood composition at one or multiple radii
categorical_marks.input: Aligned typed marks, cell IDs/coordinates/frame, levels or complete probability simplex, radius and declared null/support semantics.
categorical_marks.output: Co-occurrence/mixing matrices, compositions/diversity, weighted pair curves, bounds or permutation inference.
categorical_marks.used_by: marklab::marks and exported workflow nodes; numerics categorical-co-occurrence/enrichment and project categorical-pair expose selected methods. Most soft/ordinal methods are library building blocks; soft neighborhoods feed pathology maps.
uses: Retain uncertainty when only top-1 probabilities are available
categorical_marks.limits: Complete-simplex analyses require complete probabilities; top-1 bounds do not invent them. Co-occurrence is descriptive; enrichment count/moment agreement does not validate every Monte Carlo/null design. No learned niche clustering.

does: Continuous product-weighted K and unweighted baseline
KSG mutual information with permutation, block or variogram-matching spatial null
continuous_and_probability_marks.input: Finite aligned scalar/probability marks and spatial design; mutual information takes two measurements and its null settings.
continuous_and_probability_marks.output: Weighted curves, dependence summaries, envelopes/p-values or MI/null effect summaries.
continuous_and_probability_marks.used_by: marklab::marks and method-specific AnalysisNode types; numerics mutual-information. Probability marks also feed the marked-section spectrum.
uses: Nonlinear dependence between two cell measurements
continuous_and_probability_marks.limits: Probabilities, continuous values and hard labels have distinct contracts. Spatial MI can reflect shared regional context; reference/calibration evidence is scoped and includes a documented tie-breaking mismatch.

does: Global Moran I and Geary C
Local multivariate Moran with locationwise and global Max-T inference
Scalar empirical semivariogram and ERL envelope
Binary, including-isolates and row-standardized weight policies
autocorrelation_and_variograms.input: Scalar marks or complete multivariate rows, fixed points/window, radius or lag bins, weights, optional strata and permutations.
autocorrelation_and_variograms.output: Global/local association, null expectations, p-values, corrected local tests or lag/pair/semivariance curves.
autocorrelation_and_variograms.used_by: marklab::autocorrelation; study and pathology maps; numerics local-multivariate-moran; project local-multivariate-moran/scalar-variogram.
autocorrelation_and_variograms.limits: Local whole-row unconditional shuffling and population variance differ from default conditional LISA. Prespecify scaling/radius/strata. Public cohort evidence is scoped to binary symmetric weights including isolates.

does: Region-specific intensity for K/L and g
compartments.input: Window and nonoverlapping compartment polygons in one frame; aligned histologic labels and radius where cells are used.
compartments.output: Interface profiles, mixing/contact fractions, fragmentation and compartment-conditioned spatial summaries.
compartments.used_by: marklab::compartments and workflow nodes; project piecewise-compartment methods and pathology spatial-study share partition geometry. Pathology maps separately profiles supplied annotations using common window geometry.
compartments.limits: Regions/classes are supplied upstream. Fragmentation alone cannot report cell mixing. Synthetic geometry and scoped SPIAT mixing agreement do not establish cohort performance.

does: Ordinary kriging with declared exponential/spherical/Gaussian variogram and block-held-out checks
Landy-Szalay pair excess from a declared random catalog
Mapper graph with one-dimensional lens, overlapping cover and single-link clusters
Unmarked rectangular-window structure factor, H and alpha
structure_descriptors.input: Points, scalar fields, vectors or binary masks with declared window/pixel size, scale grid, lens, variogram or random catalog as applicable.
structure_descriptors.output: Dispersion, field predictions/variance, orientation order, scaling/gap summaries, excess-pair curve, Mapper graph or structure-factor descriptors.
structure_descriptors.used_by: marklab::structure and numerics descriptor commands; scalar variograms can inform a user-declared kriging model, but there is no automatic variogram fitting.
structure_descriptors.limits: Kriging assumes constant mean/stationary isotropy. Mapper has a 1-D lens and no stability inference. H/alpha lack uncertainty and require a fully observed rectangle. Descriptive scaling is not proof of fractality/hyperuniformity. Mark spectra and unmarked structure factors are distinct.

does: H&E/IHC cell matching and fused-cell records
multimodal_registration_and_neighborhood.input: H&E classes, IHC measurements, calibrated sections/windows and corresponding landmarks.
multimodal_registration_and_neighborhood.output: Registration/fusion diagnostics, graph-neighborhood summaries, interaction curves and territory outputs.
multimodal_registration_and_neighborhood.used_by: MultimodalEngine -> multimodal analyze/batch -> multimodal prepost. Factor-model commands below are separate workflows, not automatic stages of analyze.
multimodal_registration_and_neighborhood.limits: Registration and matching uncertainty can affect every downstream statistic. Neighborhood adjacency does not prove signaling or biological cell identity.

does: Per-marker Moran I and Geary C
Equal patient weighting after slide means
multiplex_study.input: Study recipe with numeric/binary/categorical channels, slides, windows, patient/group IDs, radius/weight policy and inference design.
multiplex_study.output: Cached slide/patient results plus result.json, report.md and manifest.
multiplex_study.used_by: study run/describe; Python run_study; Rust analyze/execute/publish_multiplex_study.
uses: Compare spatial protein organization between patient groups
multiplex_study.limits: Categorical channels are retained but not treated as numeric autocorrelation marks. Missing marker values alter the analyzed graph. Unavailable required slide results suppress that marker's patient test. Experimental scope is the documented binary-symmetric-including-isolates design.

pathology_maps.input: Calibrated cell markers/phenotypes, observation windows, supplied annotations and declared radii/distance bands.
pathology_maps.output: JSON/report plus per-slide SVG and per-cell GeoJSON map layers.
pathology_maps.used_by: pathology maps; Rust analyze_pathology_maps/publish_pathology_maps compose clipped annotation-offset geometry, soft-neighborhood composition and local Moran.
uses: Local Ki67 or other marker hotspots
pathology_maps.limits: Annotations and measurements are supplied upstream. Local maps are within-slide summaries, not independent patient observations.

does: Patient cell-type fractions and area-normalized density
Geometric balances and amalgamated log ratios
Joint patient Max-T and within-group bootstrap intervals
pathology_composition.input: Typed cells, patient/group/slide IDs, windows, declared log-ratio groups and grid designs.
pathology_composition.output: Patient and contrast tables, grid GeoJSON, MAUP SVG, JSON and report.
pathology_composition.used_by: pathology composition pools counts/areas across each patient's slides before group inference.
uses: Separate relative composition from absolute density
Check whether regional heterogeneity depends on sampling-grid choices
pathology_composition.limits: No automatic pseudocounts for zeros. Unavailable endpoints are excluded from the family without silently dropping patients. Marginal bootstrap intervals are not simultaneous intervals.

does: Intensity-adjusted L-r, g-1 and directed cross-g-1
Gaussian plug-in or refitted simulation nulls
Area-weighted patient curves and functional group tests
pathology_spatial_study.input: Typed cells/windows, patient/group declarations, common radii, intensity/edge/null/support settings and optional compartment geometry.
pathology_spatial_study.output: Slide/patient curves, null-curves.json, curve plots, JSON and report; separate within-slide, across-slide and patient-group inference.
pathology_spatial_study.used_by: pathology spatial-study composes spatial intensity, pair statistics, simulation envelopes and cohort curve inference.
uses: Compare patient groups' clustering after accounting for density
pathology_spatial_study.limits: Spatial simulations condition on counts; theoretical Poisson reference curves are not the finite-count null. No dropping or interpolating unsupported radii/patients. Fixed-bandwidth rectangular observed L-r has Experimental evidence; other configurations remain Research.

does: Cell-centered circular search across declared radii
pathology_scan.input: Target phenotype, eligible cells, strata, windows and prespecified scan radii.
pathology_scan.output: Best circle per slide, enrichment/test results, strata tables, SVG/GeoJSON, JSON and report.
pathology_scan.used_by: pathology scan searches and re-searches within each slide; it does not perform a patient-group hotspot comparison.
uses: Detect unusually concentrated immune or abnormal-cell regions
pathology_scan.limits: Only the best qualifying circle is tested; secondary clusters are not. A scan circle is not a lesion boundary, and may span disconnected tissue.

does: Invasive-front derivation with exclusions and declared-front distance agreement
Signed front-distance bands and exact region overlap areas
ITBCC-style budding candidates, front-constrained hotspot and Bd grade
Cell attachment and spatial-transcriptomic spot coverage fractions
pathology_architecture.input: Calibrated tissue/epithelium/architecture-region polygons, provenance, optional lumen/mucin/front layers, epithelial cell labels/nuclear measurements and registered circular spots.
pathology_architecture.output: Component/band/cell/spot tables, front/bulk GeoJSON and complete JSON result.
pathology_architecture.used_by: pathology architecture; Rust analyze/publish; Python QuPath annotation conversion and run_pathology_architecture. Spot IDs provide an explicit join to external expression/protein tables.
uses: Quantify glandular/solid/fragmented architecture along an invasive front
Compare morphology and registered cell states
Describe mixed tissue coverage of capture spots
pathology_architecture.limits: No epithelial segmentation or class prediction. Region overlap uses geometric areas; whole-component class uses its interior point. Budding depends on supplied components/nuclei and lacks pathologist validation. Nuclear alignment is a shape descriptor, not a force measurement.

embedding_artifacts_and_scales.input: Externally generated finite vectors, exact object links, coordinates/footprints, source declarations and optional overlap weights.
embedding_artifacts_and_scales.output: Bound and verified multiscale embedding artifacts, linkage/QC and dispersion summaries.
embedding_artifacts_and_scales.used_by: marklab::embeddings and marklab-embeddings; verified artifact graphs feed cell/patch/region analysis rather than relying on row position alone.
uses: Connect morphology features across cell, patch and slide scales
Avoid counting overlapping patches as independent support
Preserve exact identity during vector import and aggregation
embedding_artifacts_and_scales.limits: No encoder inference/training. Internal columnar profiles intentionally reject arbitrary Arrow/Parquet schemas. Aggregation requires explicit support and producer declarations.

does: Embedding-feature and cross-modal covariance by distance
Embedding kernels and kernel mark correlation
embedding_spatial_analysis.input: Identity-aligned cell/patch vectors, coordinates, distance bins or kernels, mark/morphology values and declared support/splits.
embedding_spatial_analysis.output: Spatial curves, covariance matrices, kernel artifacts, contrasts, dispersion metrics or ranked analogous regions.
embedding_spatial_analysis.used_by: marklab::embeddings and marklab-embeddings::analysis; bayes embedding commands expose descriptive computations as well as models; selected project routes add caching.
uses: Compare morphology with measured protein patterns
Assess which spatial scales carry feature dependence
embedding_spatial_analysis.limits: A bayes command prefix does not imply Bayesian inference. Unweighted observed vector semivariograms have scoped Experimental agreement; other extensions remain Research. Vector dimensions/features and preprocessing must be comparable.

does: Spatial latent factors with dense GP or SPDE prior
Dropout-robust factors and joint pathology models
Patient-level nested ridge comparisons of baseline/cell/patch/neighborhood/measured features
multimodal_factor_and_complementarity_mo.input: Declared aligned modality matrices/tensors, hierarchy/spatial support, missingness and patient training/held-out design.
multimodal_factor_and_complementarity_mo.output: Factors/loadings, shared variation, model diagnostics or held-out complementarity comparisons.
multimodal_factor_and_complementarity_mo.used_by: multimodal model commands; multimodal compare-models and bayes test-cell-patch-complementarity; durable project counterpart for complementarity.
uses: Test whether cells and patches add distinct predictive information
Compare feature scales under patient-held-out evaluation
multimodal_factor_and_complementarity_mo.limits: Separate from multimodal analyze; no automatic factor fitting in the basic registration workflow. Factors are not validated cell states, learned niches or causal mechanisms.

does: Laplacian spectral basis and frequency-band energies
Dirichlet energy, permutation smoothness and local embedding roughness
graph_analysis.input: Declared weighted graphs/signals or physical points/radius; optional edge types, hyperedges, triangles/incidence, strata and perturbations.
graph_analysis.output: Operators, spectra, energies, diffused signals, multiscale features, stability, motifs, group centrality or signal decompositions.
graph_analysis.used_by: marklab-graph; graph commands; bayes graph-signal/embedding commands; selected sparse/signal/motif project routes. graph validate exercises mathematical oracles.
graph_analysis.limits: Graph construction is part of the hypothesis. No individual betweenness or learned niche/community model. Observed group scores have Experimental evidence; other graph features remain Research and lack calibrated tissue-cohort interpretation.

topology.input: Physical points or persistence diagrams with patient labels; masks/pixel size/connectivity; declared filtrations, landmarks and perturbations.
topology.output: Simplices and birth/death pairs, diagram summaries/comparisons, stability distances, mask morphology or connectivity transitions.
topology.used_by: marklab-topology types/native connectivity; topology CLI orchestrates GUDHI persistence and scikit-image morphology workers; witness workflows have project routes.
uses: Connected clusters and loops across scales
Patient-level comparison of declared topological features
topology.limits: GUDHI is the persistence implementation, not an independent validation oracle. Features are not automatically anatomical structures or biomarkers; pixel conventions affect raster topology.

nonrigid_registration.input: Images or corresponding landmarks with explicit frames/spacing, deformation settings and uncertainty model.
nonrigid_registration.output: Transforms/deformations, alignment and uncertainty diagnostics or registered atlas.
nonrigid_registration.used_by: registration commands use Python workers; separate spatial3d workflows explicitly propagate registration uncertainty into serial/longitudinal K analyses.
uses: Assess how registration affects spatial conclusions
nonrigid_registration.limits: Correspondence is assumed or modeled. Deformation alone cannot distinguish biological change from cutting/mounting artifacts.

does: Registered longitudinal voxel-K change with deformation/control draws
spatial_3d.input: Calibrated 3-D points, cuboid/voxel window and spacing, types/intensities/uncertainty; advanced workflows add section registration, transforms, draws or clone records.
spatial_3d.output: K/cross curves, voxel geometry, spatial graph, registered-volume/change diagnostics, alpha topology or clone-location contrasts.
spatial_3d.used_by: marklab-spatial3d; flat spatial3d CLI routes; project caches four principal K workflows. Registered analyses run the same voxel K engine after declared coordinate mapping.
spatial_3d.limits: No independent 3-D K comparison or validated serial-section patient cohort. Window must represent actual observation. Registration draws/controls are explicit inputs; no same-cell tracking or causal change claim. Bayesian GP inverse-square anisotropy output cannot directly serve as dimensionless K anisotropy.

does: Functional L2 permutation and simultaneous equivalence
Multisite fixed/REML random-effects synthesis and covariate contrasts
Patient-nested field reduction and Max-T calibration
cohort_inference.input: Declared patient endpoints or curves plus groups, pairs, blocks, clusters, sites, covariates, hierarchy and prespecified margins where applicable.
cohort_inference.output: Effects, p-values/adjusted families, uncertainty intervals, heterogeneity/sensitivity, distances and patient summaries.
cohort_inference.used_by: marklab-cohort; cohort CLI; selected project routes; integrated study/pathology workflows. Other spatial/model endpoints require explicit patient-level aggregation and compatible tables.
uses: Compare multivariate or functional tissue signatures
cohort_inference.limits: Cells are not cohort replicates. Exchangeability and covariate/block designs must match sampling. Two-group Max-T has scoped Experimental evidence; other designs remain Research. Nonsignificance is not equivalence.

does: Conjugate normal mean and Gaussian patient hierarchy
Ordinal/group-site/nonproportional ordinal models and whole-site holdout
Gaussian crossed/nested effects and variance partition
bayesian_hierarchies.input: Counts, continuous/ordered outcomes and grouping/covariate data with declared priors and fitting controls.
bayesian_hierarchies.output: Posterior effects/uncertainty, model diagnostics and model-specific predictive/sensitivity results.
bayesian_hierarchies.used_by: marklab-bayes models; bayes commands invoke model-specific workers; selected fits have project counterparts. Agreement/SBC/sensitivity exist only for the named command variants.
bayesian_hierarchies.limits: Research evidence is model-specific. Nonconverged fits remain diagnostic. Variance partition is a mean share of random-effect/residual variance, not R-squared or fixed-effect variance.

does: GP regression, multi-output and anisotropic 3-D GP
Variational GP, predictive-process and NNGP approximations
Adaptive polygon-window and nonstationary anisotropic SPDE
bayesian_spatial_fields.input: Spatial outcomes/covariates, coordinates or adjacency, optional mesh, priors and resource constraints.
bayesian_spatial_fields.output: Field/effect predictions, density/likelihood values or fitted posterior/optimization summaries according to the command.
bayesian_spatial_fields.used_by: bayes field/SPDE commands; selected project routes; dense GP/SPDE priors also support multimodal spatial factors.
bayesian_spatial_fields.limits: Some density/build commands evaluate or construct models without fitting. Anisotropic GP needs identifiable axis scales; its inverse-square plug-in metric has physical units. Approximation/mesh assumptions and convergence remain explicit.

does: Covariate-dependent Poisson likelihood/fit and Berman-Turner refinement
Replicated multitype and correlated multitype LGCP
Conditional multitype marks at fixed locations
Geyer saturation and multitype Papangelou intensities
Posterior predictive point patterns and spatial checks
bayesian_point_processes.input: Locations/types/marks, observation windows, covariates/quadrature, replication and priors or declared process parameters.
bayesian_point_processes.output: Likelihood/model specification, posterior intensity/mark/cluster summaries, generated patterns or predictive diagnostics.
bayesian_point_processes.used_by: bayes point-process/build/fit commands; selected project routes cache polygon/replicated models; posterior checks compare generated and observed spatial summaries.
uses: Separate abundance/intensity from conditional mark organization
bayesian_point_processes.limits: Build commands do not imply a completed fit. Gibbs statistics/pseudolikelihood are not a general exact continuous-space Gibbs posterior. Dense Thomas fits can mix slowly; a real-data location-embedding fit did not converge. Research scope remains model-specific.

inference_and_model_checks.input: Declared observations/models or posterior log likelihoods; priors, simulation scenarios, quadrature and diagnostic criteria.
inference_and_model_checks.output: Approximate/posterior summaries, LOO scores/Pareto diagnostics, calibration ranks/coverage, agreement/sensitivity or predictive discrepancies.
inference_and_model_checks.used_by: bayes named inference and check commands wrap specific models; validation tools are not generic proof of every model's accuracy.
inference_and_model_checks.limits: Sampling convergence, backend agreement, SBC and public-cohort validity are different evidence. An implemented check is not a claim it passed on the user's data.

does: Full, partial and unbalanced fused Gromov-Wasserstein
optimal_transport.input: Source/target masses and feature/cross-costs; FGW adds within-set geometry and declared feature/structure scales.
optimal_transport.output: Couplings/assignments, matched/unmatched mass, objective/convergence and multistart diagnostics.
optimal_transport.used_by: marklab-transport; bayes transport commands; project fused-gromov-wasserstein. Basic Sinkhorn is native; FGW uses POT and partial OT uses SciPy.
uses: Allow partial overlap or changing total mass
optimal_transport.limits: Coupling is not cell identity. FGW is nonconvex and uses multiple starts; unbalanced zero-mass collapse errors. No calibrated biological correspondence test.

prediction.input: Patient-level scores/features/labels with explicit training/calibration/test splits; out-of-fold base predictions for fusion.
prediction.output: Calibrated probabilities/sets/coverage, OOD and abstention decisions, fusion/gating weights and held-out performance diagnostics.
prediction.used_by: marklab-prediction; bayes prediction commands consume declared upstream model outputs. Region retrieval is a separate embedding workflow.
prediction.limits: Coverage/calibration depend on split/exchangeability assumptions. Base predictions must satisfy the declared out-of-fold contract. No demonstrated clinical safety or general real-cohort predictive validity.

does: Vessel-source transport in a static flow field
simulation.input: Windows/grids, initial states, equations/parameters, boundary/numerical settings, seeds and budgets.
simulation.output: Synthetic cells, trajectories/states, solver diagnostics or weighted summary losses.
simulation.used_by: marklab-simulation and simulate CLI; the Fisher-KPP solver is directly consumed by growth-front SBI. Point-process simulators are also exposed under bayes.
simulation.limits: Equations and parameters are hypotheses; summary matching does not identify or validate a mechanism in real tissue.

simulation_based_inference.input: Observed summaries, Fisher-KPP initial state/design, prior/tolerance and simulation/particle budgets.
simulation_based_inference.output: Accepted/weighted posterior draws, support decisions, calibration or predictive checks.
simulation_based_inference.used_by: marklab-sbi -> marklab-simulation Fisher-KPP; bayes growth-front inference commands; project smc-abc-growth-front caches the SMC route.
uses: Check whether observations lie within simulator support
Assess recovery and posterior fit on synthetic controls
simulation_based_inference.limits: Current workflows are specific simulator/summary contracts. Similar summaries may come from different parameters or mechanisms.

does: Neural point-process intensity and categorical marks
neural_models.input: Point patterns/windows, patient splits/context or declared simulations/priors with architecture/training/resource settings.
neural_models.output: Intensity/mark predictions, generated patterns, posterior summaries or generative diagnostics.
neural_models.used_by: neural CLI orchestrates locked JAX/torch/sbi or model-specific workers.
neural_models.limits: This family does not train image encoders. Synthetic checks do not establish tissue posterior coverage or real-cohort performance.

causal_designs.input: Treatment/outcomes, units/clusters, covariates, interference graph and explicit identification/design assumptions.
causal_designs.output: Effects/exposures, sensitivity curves/bounds, information gain or selected acquisitions/power diagnostics.
causal_designs.used_by: marklab-causal and causal CLI; selected project randomized-interference/gaussian-eig routes; advanced designs use Python workers.
causal_designs.limits: Requires the stated randomization/exposure/observational identification assumptions. Tissue association alone does not satisfy them.

does: Permutation association of phylogenetic and spatial distances
longitudinal.input: Repeated observations with transition/noise model, nonlinear/particle settings or clone/tree and spatial distances.
longitudinal.output: Predicted/filtered/smoothed states and uncertainty, likelihood diagnostics or distance-association inference.
longitudinal.used_by: marklab-longitudinal; longitudinal CLI; project longitudinal-kalman-smooth. Registered 3-D timepoint change is a separate spatial3d flow.
longitudinal.limits: Conditional on the declared dynamical/noise model; no real repeated-patient clinical validation or same-cell tracking.

does: Normalized weighted means and two-pass covariance
numerical_foundation.input: Finite vectors/matrices/weights or aligned observed/null curves with explicit size/work limits.
numerical_foundation.output: Stable numerical summaries/solutions or explicit singular/unavailable failures; global-envelope depths/bounds/p-values.
numerical_foundation.used_by: marklab-numerics underlies spatial sums, covariance, graph/kernel/kriging computations and ERL inference; numerics stable-primitives exposes selected operations.
uses: Custom Rust analyses using the same numerical policies
Method checks against known small problems
numerical_foundation.limits: Primitives are not separate scientific models; numerical stability is not evidence of biological validity.

does: Typed workflow DAG and local scheduler
Compatible result caching and dependent invalidation
durable_execution_and_policy.input: Declared nodes, dependencies, input artifacts, algorithm/runtime identity, seeds and resource limits; policy decisions consume declared evidence flags.
durable_execution_and_policy.output: Stored artifacts, node/run/cache/recovery status, completed reports or policy decisions.
durable_execution_and_policy.used_by: project's explicit command subset, study run and public workflow nodes; backend doctor checks the installed worker runtime.
durable_execution_and_policy.limits: No universal automatic pipeline connecting all commands. Cached execution and declared policy flags do not promote scientific validity. The scheduler is local, not a distributed service.

does: GUDHI, scikit-image, POT, SimpleITK, MOFA, CCA and neural workers
Isolated process environment and bounded execution
Compatible saved-result reuse without new backend execution
python_backend_runtime.input: Worker assets, locked environment, serialized requests and explicit runtime/cache configuration.
python_backend_runtime.output: Identity-checked worker results, version/runtime diagnostics or explicit failure.
python_backend_runtime.used_by: Model-specific CLI orchestration and durable project nodes. MARKLAB_RUNTIME_ROOT, MARKLAB_PYTHON, MARKLAB_BACKEND_CACHE and MARKLAB_BACKEND_PATH configure execution; MARKLAB_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_BACKEND_EXECUTION blocks new launches.
uses: Run selected external scientific implementations reproducibly
python_backend_runtime.limits: Doctor checks installation/versions, not numerical accuracy, model suitability or GPU support. Linux is the CI reference; all families retain their own evidence and platform limits.

interactions.flow: Upstream segmentation/classification -> calibrated cells + observed window -> marked analysis -> batch/prepost
interactions.note: Upstream image modeling is external; batch shares configuration, and prepost compares completed compatible analyses.

interactions.flow: H&E + IHC + landmarks -> registration -> fused cells -> graph -> enrichment/cross-curves/territories
interactions.note: The basic multimodal pipeline; registration quality affects downstream interpretation.

interactions.flow: Multiplex cells -> per-marker slide autocorrelation -> patient means -> Max-T report
interactions.note: study runs and caches the complete chain; each patient counts once.

interactions.flow: Typed patient slides -> composition/grid sensitivity or intensity-adjusted curves -> patient-group inference
interactions.note: pathology composition and spatial-study use different pooling and null designs.

interactions.flow: Annotated structures + cells -> interface distances/neighborhood composition/local Moran -> maps
interactions.note: pathology maps produces physical-coordinate SVG/GeoJSON layers.

interactions.flow: Epithelium + declared regions -> bulk/front/bands -> architecture/nuclei/buds/spot coverage
interactions.note: pathology architecture; spot-expression joins occur downstream using explicit spot IDs.

interactions.flow: Cell/patch vectors + exact links -> multiscale support -> spatial features or held-out complementarity
interactions.note: Artifacts and individual methods exist; callers choose compatible feature definitions and patient splits.

interactions.flow: Section/graph/topology/embedding features -> patient endpoints -> cohort/Bayesian/prediction models
interactions.note: Requires declared endpoint construction and aggregation; arbitrary output JSON is not an automatic next-command input.

interactions.flow: Growth-front simulator -> ABC/synthetic likelihood -> posterior-predictive and support checks
interactions.note: The SBI growth-front routes directly call the native simulator.

interactions.flow: Registered serial/longitudinal sections -> coordinate uncertainty -> voxel-window 3-D K/change
interactions.note: Dedicated spatial3d routes propagate the declared registration uncertainty.

interactions.flow: Scientific command -> admitted node -> local artifact store -> compatible cache reuse
interactions.note: Only listed project routes and public workflow nodes have this execution path.

applications.question: Is MMR-loss or another binary stain spatially organized?
applications.scope: Observed-label organization; not molecular diagnosis or clonality.

applications.question: Are immune and tumor cells mixed, excluded or concentrated near the border?
applications.scope: Choose annotation, edge and null conventions before inference.

applications.question: Does organization differ between patient groups after accounting for abundance?
applications.scope: Keep composition/density and spatial-interaction hypotheses distinct.

applications.question: Which proteins have different spatial patterns across patients?
applications.scope: Explicit observed channels, graph weights and independent patients.

applications.question: How does architecture vary across an invasive front?
applications.scope: Architecture computation is integrated; patient endpoint construction/group testing requires explicit orchestration.

applications.question: How do morphology and molecular measurements relate across space and scale?
applications.scope: Matched identities or declared registration and patient-held-out evaluation.

applications.question: How do capture spots mix architecture classes?
applications.scope: Join coverage fractions to external expression by spot ID; expression normalization and deconvolution are external.

applications.question: Which regions should be reviewed or compared with analogous tissue?
Do patterns persist across sections, time or three dimensions?
applications.scope: Distinct sections/timepoints need explicit coordinate and sampling models.

applications.question: Could a hypothesized mechanism generate the observed organization?
applications.scope: Model checking and hypothesis generation; similar summaries do not identify a mechanism.

applications.question: Do multiple modalities improve patient predictions?
applications.scope: Patient-held-out calibration/fusion/OOD/abstention, without a clinical-performance claim.

applications.question: How should a perturbation or acquisition study be designed?
applications.scope: Requires declared intervention, interference and identification assumptions.

applications.question: Can these methods describe other marked point patterns?
applications.scope: Possible after explicit mapping to supported geometry/marks/units; non-pathology validation is not claimed.

evidence.default: Research: implemented with method-specific synthetic/analytic checks and documented assumptions; no blanket tissue-cohort validation.
experimental_examples: Observed categorical co-occurrence and enrichment counts/exact moments
Specified global Moran/Geary and multiplex study configurations
evidence.core: No workflow currently meets every documented Core criterion.

real_data_examples.Jackson_IMC: 100 patients; composition/Max-T evidence, not spatial-arrangement validation.
real_data_examples.other: Published retinal point patterns, PUMA QuPath nuclei, MCMICRO tonsil and STHELAR CellViT vectors provide method/adapter-specific evidence.

known_gaps: Fitted-null and irregular-window calibration is configuration-specific
Local Moran's unconditional null differs from default conditional LISA
Bayesian Thomas dense-aggregate fits can mix slowly
Real-data joint location-embedding pilot did not converge
No clinical diagnosis, outcome or mechanism validity follows from software tests
Windows binaries lack end-to-end testing; Python CI reference is Linux

external_upstream: Physical calibration and biological identity declarations
not_implemented_as_native_pipelines: Multidimensional Mapper lenses and 3-D Steinhardt order
boundaries.planned_adapter: Native HoVer-Net JSON; not currently a supported import path.
not_established: Diagnosis, molecular MMR status or treatment response
Clinical safety from calibrated probabilities or abstention

project.note: Only these explicit project routes are available; other public AnalysisNode types may be composed in Rust.

bayes.note: All listed commands are flat under bayes; names such as vector-semivariogram also include descriptive non-Bayesian computations.

crate_map.marklab: Primary marked, spatial, pathology, multimodal, IO and CLI workflows.
crate_map.marklab-data: Cohort hierarchy, coordinate frames/transforms, replication and measurement contracts.
crate_map.marklab-embeddings: Bound vector artifacts, multiscale links and embedding analyses.
crate_map.marklab-cohort: Patient-level tests, pooling, multiplicity, margins and bootstrap.
crate_map.marklab-bayes: Model specifications, workers, posterior and validation contracts.
crate_map.marklab-prediction: Retrieval, calibration/fusion, conformal and prediction safeguards.
crate_map.marklab-spatial3d: Volumetric spatial geometry/statistics and advanced worker protocols.
crate_map.marklab-numerics: Stable reductions, kernels, matrix solvers and envelopes.
crate_map.marklab-project: Artifact storage, publication, identity, recovery and durable runs.
crate_map.marklab-workflow: Typed DAGs, local scheduling and caching execution.
crate_map.marklab-policy: Declared maturity, execution-mode and validation-ladder decisions.
